subject: Follow-up: reliability / SLO comparison vs hyperscalers — PoC kickoff and test plan
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: reliability / SLO comparison vs hyperscalers — next tests

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the call today — good to learn more about Acme's inference surface and reliability priorities. Quick recap and proposed next steps so everyone is aligned: 

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary goal: reduce service-level risk for production LLM features (chat & summarization) while keeping unit cost predictable.
- Key SLOs: p95 latency target ~200ms for short-form queries, 99.9% uptime, and defined error budget per month.
- Traffic: mixed bursty behavior with sustained 400–600 RPS and peaks to ~2k RPS during campaigns.
- Concerned about: regional failover behavior and per-account rate limits on hyperscaler endpoints.

What Redwood proposes next
1) Technical test plan: run a 72-hour comparative test (Redwood vs HyperscalerX public API) using a replay of a representative traffic sample. We'll measure p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, throttling events, cold-start behavior, and actual failover behavior during simulated region disruption.
2) Deliverables: a short results deck with SLO headroom analysis, error-budget burn curves, and concrete recommendations for routing/fallback policies.
3) Logistics: need a traffic sample (tokenized requests or anonymized request log) and a preferred test week.

Attached: 20260304-reliability-slo-comparison.pdf — short overview of the metrics we'll capture.

Proposed timeline
- Please confirm a test week (we suggested Mar 8–12 on the call).
- Share the traffic sample or a synthetic profile by EOD Tue Mar 3.

Cc'ing Marissa (customer success) and Rishi (SRE) to help scope the technical test.

Thanks —
Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0132

Attachment: 20260304-reliability-slo-comparison.pdf (PDF, 2 pages)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: reliability / SLO comparison vs hyperscalers — next tests

Hi Alex —

Quick technical clarifications to make sure our test captures the behaviors you care about: 

1) Latency buckets: we'll report p50/p90/p95/p99 for both cold and warm paths. Please confirm if the 200ms p95 target you mentioned is for the warm path only or needs to include cold-starts.

2) Rate limits and throttling: Redwood exposes per-customer rate limits that are configurable. For the test we'll run at the following ramps:
   - Sustained: 500 RPS
   - Burst: 2k RPS for 5–10 minute windows
   - Concurrency: up to 200 concurrent connections

3) Error budget definition: we'll compute monthly error budget as 1 - availability SLO (e.g., 0.1% for 99.9%) and show burn-rate both as raw downtime and as request-failure fraction. We'll also include simulated degradations (e.g., model throttling vs full regional outage) to observe automatic fallback behaviour.

4) Failover behaviour: Redwood's smart routing can do region fallback to a warm replica and/or fallback to a lower-cost model variant with graceful degradation. For the test we'll run a controlled failover during a low-traffic window and capture failover time, error spike, and successful requests during the event.

5) Data needed from you: an anonymized request log with typical request sizes (token counts), at least 1 hour of peak traffic and 4 hours of typical traffic. CSV is fine (we can accept s3 link).

Attached is a more detailed test plan file (redwood-test-plan.yaml) that includes the exact metrics and thresholds we'll record.

If this looks good I'll sync with infra to provision the dedicated test capacity and provide credentials.

Thanks,
Rishi
SRE Lead | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

---
Attachment: redwood-test-plan.yaml (YAML, 3KB)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: reliability / SLO comparison vs hyperscalers — next tests

Thanks Ben and Rishi — this looks helpful. A few answers / clarifications from our side: 

- The 200ms p95 is our target for the warm path. Cold-starts are allowed to be higher for model loads, but we'd like to measure both.
- Traffic sample: uploading a ~2k row sample to the bucket now: s3://acme-test/traffic-sample.csv (contains request timestamps, token counts, and anonymized user IDs).
- Our typical sustained is ~400–600 RPS, peak bursts up to ~2k for marketing pushes. Concurrency-wise we can confirm up to 250 concurrent in practice.
- Error budget: our execs think in terms of monthly uptime (99.9%) and want to see projected cost of improving to 99.95%. Please include a rough cost delta in the results deck.
- Failover question: what happens if the primary region becomes unreachable for >10 minutes? Do you automatically route to another region, or is there a manual intervention window? We need to understand RTO and RPO for both hosted and dedicated modes.

We can do the PoC week of Mar 8. Prefer kickoff on Mon Mar 8 at 10am PT. Can you confirm?

Thanks,
Alex
Head of Platform Engineering | Acme AI
alex.johnson@acme.ai

Alex — great, thanks for the quick turnaround and the sample. Confirming next steps and owners: 

1) Kickoff: Mon Mar 8, 10am PT — Ben (owner, logistics), Marissa (customer success lead), Rishi (technical lead). I'll send calendar invite in a sec.
2) Redwood will provision a dedicated test harness and run the 72-hour comparative tests vs HyperscalerX starting immediately after kickoff. Expect credentials and a detailed runbook by EOD Mar 5.
3) We'll include: p50/p95/p99, cold vs warm paths, error budget burn curves, failover RTO/RPO observations, and a cost delta estimate for moving SLO from 99.9% to 99.95%.
4) If you'd like, we can add a short canary test to mirror your production routing rules (sticky sessions, tokenized prefixes). Let us know preference prior to kickoff.

Attached: traffic-sample.csv (what you provided) — we'll use this for the replay.

Looking forward —
